cues.en: So, with our cautionary tale about data sparsity out of the way, let's talk about some other ways to compute similarity.
cues.zh: 提醒過資料稀疏的問題後，接著談其他計算相似度的方法。

cues.en: One is the adjusted cosine metric and its applicable mostly to measuring the similarity between users based on their ratings.
cues.zh: 一種是調整式餘弦指標，主要適合根據評分，衡量使用者之間的相似度。

cues.en: It's based on the idea that different people might have different baselines that they are working from.
cues.zh: 它的概念是，不同人的基準可能不同。

cues.en: What Bob considers a three star movie, maybe different from what Alice considers a three star movie.
cues.zh: Bob 認為是三星的電影，與 Alice 認為是三星的電影，可能不同。

cues.en: Maybe Bob is just hesitant to rate things five stars unless they are truly amazing, while Alice tries to be nice and rates things five stars unless she really didn't like them.
cues.zh: 也許 Bob 除非真的非常驚豔，否則不太願意給五星；Alice 則盡量友善，除非真的不喜歡，否則都給五星。

cues.en: This is a real effect you'll see, not just across individuals, but across different cultures too.
cues.zh: 這個現象確實存在，不只個人之間，不同文化之間也有。

cues.en: Some countries are more brutal with their ratings than others.
cues.zh: 有些國家評分比較嚴苛。

cues.en: So, adjusted cosine attempts to normalize these differences.
cues.zh: 因此，調整式餘弦試圖將這些差異正規化。

cues.en: Instead of measuring similarities between people based on their raw rating values, we instead measures similarities based on the difference between a users rating for an item, and their average rating for all items.
cues.zh: 不是根據原始評分衡量人們的相似度，而是看某位使用者對某項目的評分，與他對所有項目平均評分之間的差異。

cues.en: So, if you look at this equation, if you replace X with X sub i minus X bar, and replaced Y with Y sub i and Y bar.
cues.zh: 看這個公式，把 X 換成 X_i 減 X̄，把 Y 換成 Y_i 減 Ȳ。

cues.en: X bar means the average of all user X's ratings, and Y bar means the average of all user Y's ratings.
cues.zh: X̄ 表示使用者 X 所有評分的平均，Ȳ 表示使用者 Y 所有評分的平均。

cues.en: So, all that's different here from conventional cosine similarity is that we are looking at the variance from the mean of each users ratings, and not just the raw rating itself.
cues.zh: 因此，與一般餘弦相似度唯一差異，是看每位使用者的評分與平均的偏離，而不只是原始評分。

cues.en: Now, this sounds good on paper, but I practice, data sparsity can really mess you up here.
cues.zh: 理論上聽起來不錯，但實務上，資料稀疏可能把事情搞砸。

cues.en: You can only get a meaningful average, or a baseline of an individuals ratings if they have rated a lot of stuff for you to take the average of in the first place.
cues.zh: 只有當某個人評分過很多東西，才能算出有意義的評分平均值或基準。

cues.en: The movie lines data set that we are working with cheats a little, Because it only includes data from people who rated at least 20 movies.
cues.zh: 我們使用的 MovieLens 資料集有點取巧，因為它只包含至少評分過 20 部電影的人。

cues.en: In the real world, you might have lot of users who are new to your system, who have only rated one thing, and that data will be totally wasted with the adjusted cosine metric.
cues.zh: 真實世界中，可能有很多剛進來、只評過一項的新使用者，而調整式餘弦會完全浪費這份資料。

cues.en: No matter what they rated that one movie that they told you about, the difference between it and that users mean will be zero at that point.
cues.zh: 不管他給唯一那部電影幾分，與自己的平均評分之差，都會是零。

cues.en: So, adjusted cosine might be worth experimenting with but only if you know that most of your users have rated a lot of stuff implicitly or explicitly.
cues.zh: 因此，調整式餘弦也許值得實驗，但前提是，你知道大多數使用者已經對很多東西，提供隱含或明確評分。

cues.en: And if you have that much data to begin with, these differences between individuals will start to work themselves out anyway.
cues.zh: 而如果一開始就有那麼多資料，個人之間的差異也會開始自行抵銷。

cues.en: So, you're not likely to see as much of a difference as you might expect when using adjusted cosine.
cues.zh: 因此，使用調整式餘弦，可能不會有你預期的那麼大差異。

cues.en: A slight twist on adjusted cosine is the Pearson similarity metric.
cues.zh: 調整式餘弦的一個小變形，是皮爾森相似度。

cues.en: The only difference is that instead of looking at the difference between ratings and a users average rating, we look at the difference between ratings and the average from all users for that given item.
cues.zh: 唯一差異是，不看評分與使用者平均評分之差，而是看評分與所有使用者對該項目平均評分之差。

cues.en: So, in this equation, we've substituted X bar and Y bar, for i bar, the average rating of the item in question from across all users.
cues.zh: 因此，公式中以 ī，也就是所有使用者對目標項目的平均評分，取代 X̄ 與 Ȳ。

cues.en: So, we're no longer trying to account for an individuals personal definitions of specific ratings scores, and in a real world situation with sparse data, that's probably a good thing,
cues.zh: 我們不再試圖補償每個人對特定分數的個人定義；在稀疏資料的真實世界情況中，這可能是好事，

cues.en: but you can think of Pearson's similarity as measuring the similarity between people by how much they diverge from the average person's behavior.
cues.zh: 你可以把皮爾森相似度，想成衡量人們偏離一般人行為的程度，有多相似。

cues.en: Imagine a film that most people love, like Star Wars, people who hate Star Wars are going to get a very strong similarity score from Pearson's similarity because they share opinions that are not mainstream.
cues.zh: 想像一部大多數人喜愛的電影，例如《星際大戰》。討厭它的人，會得到很高的皮爾森相似度，因為他們共享非主流的看法。

cues.en: Note that the only difference between this and adjusted cosine is whether we're talking about users or items.
cues.zh: 注意，它與調整式餘弦的唯一差異，是談使用者還是項目。

cues.en: The surprise library we are using in this course, refers to adjusted cosine as user based Pearson's similarity, because it's basically the same thing.
cues.zh: 本課程使用的 Surprise 函式庫，把調整式餘弦稱為使用者式皮爾森相似度，因為基本上是同一件事。

cues.en: Which can be a little bit confusing The Pearson similarity we're talking about in this slide, is what they call item based Pearson similarity.
cues.zh: 這可能有點混淆。本投影片所說的皮爾森相似度，在它那裡叫做項目式皮爾森相似度。

cues.en: Surprise, this documentation also uses slightly notation than we do, but if you break it down, its the same idea.
cues.zh: Surprise 文件使用的符號，也與我們略有不同，但拆解後，概念相同。

cues.en: Making sense of notation is often half of the battle of understanding these algorithms.
cues.zh: 理解符號，往往就是理解演算法的一半工作。

cues.en: For completeness, I'm going to briefly mention Spearman rank correlation as well.
cues.zh: 為求完整，也簡單提一下斯皮爾曼等級相關。

cues.en: At a conceptional level, it's the same idea as Pearson's similarity, but instead of using ratings scores directly, we use ranks instead.
cues.zh: 概念上與皮爾森相似度相同，但不直接使用評分，而是使用排名。

cues.en: That is, instead of using an average rating value for a movie, we'd use its rank amongst all movies based on their average ratings.
cues.zh: 也就是，不用電影的平均評分，而是用它在所有電影中，根據平均評分得到的排名。

cues.en: And, instead of individual ratings for a movie, we'd rank that movie amongst all that individuals ratings.
cues.zh: 同樣地，不用某人給電影的個別評分，而是看它在這個人的所有評分中，排在什麼位置。

cues.en: I'm not going to go into the details on this because it's going to confuse you, the math gets tricky, its very computationally intensive and its generally not worth it.
cues.zh: 這裡不深入細節，因為會讓人混淆，數學複雜、運算成本很高，而且通常不值得。

cues.en: The main advantage of Spearman, is that it can deal with ordinal data effectively.
cues.zh: 斯皮爾曼的主要優點，是能有效處理次序資料。

cues.en: For example, if you had a ratings scale where the difference in meaning between different rating values were not the same.
cues.zh: 例如，評分量表中，不同評分值之間的意義差距並不相等。

cues.en: I've never seen this actually used in real world applications myself, but, you may encounter it in the academic literature.
cues.zh: 我自己從沒看過它實際用於真實應用，但學術文獻中可能會遇到。

cues.en: Another way to measure similarity, is the mean squared difference similarity metric, ad it's exactly what it sounds like.
cues.zh: 另一個相似度衡量方式，是均方差相似度，意義正如名稱。

cues.en: You look at, say, all of the items that two users have in common in their ratings, and compute the mean of the square differences between how each user rated each item.
cues.zh: 例如，查看兩位使用者共同評分的所有項目，計算他們對每項評分之差的平方，再取平均。

cues.en: It's easier to wrap your head around this since it doesn't involve angles and multidimensional space.
cues.zh: 這比較容易理解，因為不涉及角度與多維空間。

cues.en: You're just directly comparing how two people rated the same set of things.
cues.zh: 只是直接比較兩個人，對同一組東西如何評分。

cues.en: It's very much the same idea of how we measure mean absolute error, when measuring the accuracy of a recommenders system as a whole.
cues.zh: 概念很像衡量整體推薦系統準確程度時，計算平均絕對誤差。

cues.en: So, if we break down that top equation, it says that the mean squared difference, or MSD for short, between two users X and Y is given by the following.
cues.zh: 拆解上面的公式，它表示兩位使用者 X 與 Y 之間的均方差，簡稱 MSD，計算如下。

cues.en: On the top of this fraction, we are summing up for every item i that users X and Y have both rated.
cues.zh: 分子對使用者 X 與 Y 都評分過的每個項目 i，加總

cues.en: The difference between the ratings from each user squared.
cues.zh: 兩位使用者評分差的平方。

cues.en: We then divide by the number of items each user had in common that we summed across to get the average or mean.
cues.zh: 再除以加總的共同項目數量，得到平均值。

cues.en: Now, the problem is that we have computed a metric of how different users X and Y are, and we want to measure how similar they are not how different they are.
cues.zh: 問題是，算出的是 X 與 Y 有多不同，而我們想衡量的是多相似，不是多不同。

cues.en: So, to do that, we just take the inverse of MSD dividing it by one, and we have to stick that plus one on the bottom in order to avoid dividing by zero in the case where these two users have identical rating behavior.
cues.zh: 因此，取 MSD 的倒數，也就是用一去除；分母要再加一，避免兩位使用者評分行為完全相同時，除以零。

cues.en: You can, by the way, flip everything we just said to apply to items instead of users, so X and Y could refer to two different things instead of two different people, and then we'd be looking at the differences in ratings
cues.zh: 順帶一提，剛才的說法也可以反過來，套用到項目而不是使用者。X 與 Y 可以指兩個不同項目，而不是兩個人，這時看的就是

cues.en: from the people these items have in common, instead of the items people have in common.
cues.zh: 兩個項目的共同使用者所給的評分差，而不是兩個使用者的共同項目。

cues.en: As we'll see shortly, there are two different ways of doing collaborative filtering.
cues.zh: 很快就會看到，協同過濾有兩種方式。

cues.en: Item based and user based, and it's important to remember that most of these similarity metrics can apply to either approach.
cues.zh: 項目式與使用者式，必須記得，大部分相似度指標都適用於兩種方法。

cues.en: So, that's MSD.
cues.zh: 這就是 MSD。

cues.en: It's easier to comprehend than cosine similarity metrics, but in practice, you'll usually find that cosine works better.
cues.zh: 比餘弦相似度容易理解，但實務上，通常會發現餘弦表現更好。

cues.en: The last similariy measure we will cover is the Jaccard similarity metric.
cues.zh: 最後介紹 Jaccard 相似度。

cues.en: Fortunately, it's really easy to wrap your head around.
cues.zh: 幸好，它非常容易理解。

cues.en: Let's imagine two users, A and B.
cues.zh: 假設有兩位使用者 A 與 B。

cues.en: The Jaccard similarity between these two users is simply the size of the intersection between these two users ratings, divided by the union of those two users ratings.
cues.zh: 他們的 Jaccard 相似度，就是兩人的評分項目交集大小，除以聯集大小。

cues.en: So, we would count up all the movies, for example, that both users indicated some sort of interest in, and divide that by the total number of movies that either user indicated interest in.
cues.zh: 例如，計算兩人都表示感興趣的電影數，除以任一人表示感興趣的電影總數。

cues.en: Since we're just counting things up, we're not looking at actual rating values at all here, which is some pretty important information to be throwing away you would think,
cues.zh: 由於只是計數，完全不看實際評分值，你可能覺得這捨棄了很重要的資訊，

cues.en: but if you are dealing with implicit ratings, for example, just the fact that somebody watched something or bought something, you might not have real rating values to work with anyhow.
cues.zh: 但如果是隱含評分，例如只知道某人看過或買過某個東西，本來就可能沒有實際評分可用。

cues.en: You just have the fact that they either did something to express interest in an item, or they didn't.
cues.zh: 只知道他有沒有做出表示對項目感興趣的行為。

cues.en: And, in that case, Jaccard can be a reasonable choice that's very fast to compute.
cues.zh: 這時，Jaccard 就是合理且計算非常快速的選擇。

cues.en: So, a quick recap on different similarity measures before we move on.
cues.zh: 繼續之前，快速回顧不同相似度衡量方式。

cues.en: Cosine similarity is a good Jack of all trades.
cues.zh: 餘弦相似度很通用。

cues.en: It's almost always a reasonable thing to start with.
cues.zh: 幾乎總是合理的起點。

cues.en: Adjusted cosine and Pearson, are two different terms for basically the same thing.
cues.zh: 調整式餘弦與皮爾森，基本上是同一件事的兩種名稱。

cues.en: It's mean centered cosine similarities at the end of the day.
cues.zh: 說到底，都是經平均值中心化的餘弦相似度。

cues.en: So, it works in average rating behavior across all of the users item ratings, or the average ratings of an item across all users depending on which way you flip it.
cues.zh: 因此，依照使用者與項目如何對調，納入某位使用者對所有項目的平均評分，或所有使用者對某項目的平均評分。

cues.en: The idea is to deal with unusual rating behavior that deviated from the mean, but in practice, it can sometimes do more harm than good.
cues.zh: 概念是處理偏離平均的特殊評分行為，但實務上，有時可能弊大於利。

cues.en: Spearman rank correlation is the same idea as Pearson, using rankings instead of raw ratings, and its not something you are likely to be using in practice.
cues.zh: 斯皮爾曼等級相關與皮爾森概念相同，用排名取代原始評分，實務上不太可能使用。

cues.en: MSD is mean squared difference, which is just an easier similarity metric to wrap your head around than cosine similarity, but in practice, it usually doesn't perform better.
cues.zh: MSD 是均方差，比餘弦相似度更容易理解，但實務上通常不會表現更好。

cues.en: Finally we talked about Jaccard similarity.
cues.zh: 最後，談過 Jaccard 相似度。

cues.en: Which is just looking at how many items two users have in common, or how may users two items have in common divided by how many items or users they have between both of them.
cues.zh: 它只看兩位使用者有多少共同項目，或兩個項目有多少共同使用者，再除以兩者總共有多少不同項目或使用者。

cues.en: It's really simple and well suited to implicit ratings, like binary actions, like purchasing or viewing something, where you either do something or you don't.
cues.zh: 非常簡單，適合購買或觀看等二元行為的隱含評分，也就是有做或沒做。

cues.en: But, you can also apply cosine similarities to implicit ratings too.
cues.zh: 但餘弦相似度，也可以套用於隱含評分。

cues.en: So, at the end of the day, cosine similarity remains my default go to similarity metric.
cues.zh: 因此，說到底，餘弦相似度仍是我預設優先使用的指標。
